steps.body: Turn a story into a graph by breaking it into stages and giving each a shape: steady increase → straight rising line, holding steady → flat, decreasing → falling line. Chain the pieces in order to sketch the whole story.

widget.prompt: A pool fills at a steady rate, then the hose is turned off (water level holds). Which graph shape fits?

segments.label: Fills steadily
segments.meaning: The output increases at a constant rate.

bank.label: straight rising line
bank.meaning: The output increases at a constant rate.

bank.label: flat horizontal segment
bank.meaning: The output does not change.

bank.label: straight falling line
bank.meaning: The output decreases at a constant rate.

bank.label: rising curve that gets steeper
bank.meaning: The output increases faster and faster.

wrongSequences.feedback: That's the reverse order — it FILLS first (rising), THEN holds (flat).
wrongSequences.label: A flat line, then rising

wrongSequences.feedback: The water never decreases here — it rises, then holds steady.
wrongSequences.label: A falling line, then rising

wrongSequences.feedback: Steady filling is a straight line, not a steepening curve — then it goes flat.
wrongSequences.label: A steep curve upward the whole time

widget.successFeedback: Right — steady filling rises steadily, then holding steady is flat.
widget.explorationFeedback: Build the graph by adding one labelled stage for each part of the story, in the same order.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Match each stage to its direction, rate, or stopped interval, then keep the story order unchanged.

predict.prompt: Before you assemble the stages, what graph feature should appear after the hose is turned off?
predict.reveal: Turning the hose off makes the water level hold steady, so the second stage must be flat. Now build both stages in order.

steps.body: The order and direction of the stages matter. 'Rises, then falls' looks different from 'falls, then rises.' Read the story left to right and lay the shapes down in the same order.

explanationVariants: A car speeds up (distance rising ever steeper), then drives steadily (straight rising line): a curve steepening, then a straight climb.
Speeding up curves upward; steady speed is a straight slanted line.

explanationVariants: Money that grows faster and faster each year is a curve getting STEEPER — nonlinear, bending upward.
Faster-and-faster growth curves upward, steepening over time.

widget.prompt: Savings grow by MORE each year than the year before. Which graph shape fits?

segments.meaning: The output increases faster and faster.

bank.label: rising curve that gets steeper
bank.meaning: The output increases faster and faster.

bank.label: straight rising line

bank.label: flat horizontal segment
bank.meaning: The output does not change.

bank.label: straight falling line

widget.successFeedback: Right — growing by more each year makes the graph curve upward, steepening.

explanationVariants: Drives fast (steep straight rise), stops at a light (flat), then drives slowly (gentle straight rise): steep line, flat, gentle line.
Three stages: steep rising, flat, gentle rising — in that order.

bank.label: flat horizontal segment

bank.label: gentle rising line

bank.label: straight falling line
bank.meaning: The output decreases at a constant rate.

wrongSequences.feedback: That reverses fast and slow — it drives FAST first (steep), then SLOW last (gentle).

wrongSequences.feedback: The car drives FIRST (steep rise), then stops (flat) — it doesn't start out stopped.
wrongSequences.label: Flat, then steep rising, then gentle rising

widget.successFeedback: Right — fast is steep, stopped is flat, slow is a gentle rise.

Direction and order of stages both matter to the final sketch.
